name: Counseling, College, and Career
blurb: Every spring, many high school graduates are admitted to college, plan to go, and never show up in the fall. Researchers call this summer melt.
title: Counseling, College, and Career
answer: Every spring, many high school graduates are admitted to college, plan to go, and never show up in the fall. Researchers call this summer melt.

papers.why: High school example of AI for career prep with dependency risk.
papers.title: Generative AI in high school English career preparation units: Student interactions, perceptions, and ethical concerns
papers.venue: Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence, vol 10
papers.finding: High school ELA units used AI for resumes and text-based mock interviews. Positive perceptions; many students questioned and revised AI output, others became passive or dependent; concerns about generic responses.

papers.why: Relevant to CTE and career pathway ideas.
papers.title: Needs and requirements for an additional AI qualification during dual vocational training: Results from studies of apprentices and teachers
papers.venue: Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence, vol 3
papers.finding: Mixed methods: 12 vocational teachers and 746 apprentices in Germany want an AI qualification covering basic AI concepts, taught blended and action-oriented.

papers.why: Supports the book's argument that AI readiness includes human capabilities.
papers.title: Rethinking the entwinement between artificial intelligence and human learning: What capabilities do learners need for a world with AI?
papers.venue: Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence, vol 3
papers.finding: Eleven-author dialogue on what capabilities learners need in a world with AI: cognitive, humanistic, and social, not only AI literacy.

papers.why: Supports teacher and student co-design in pilots.
papers.title: How can we design for learning in an AI world?
papers.venue: Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence, vol 3
papers.finding: Argues educators and learners should co-design learning for an AI world using a capability approach.

papers.title: Are Artificially Intelligent Conversational Chatbots Uniformly Effective in Reducing Summer Melt? Evidence from a Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: RCT, 4,442 admitted students: chatbot outreach helped most with financial aid steps, concentrated among first-generation students.

papers.title: Nudging at scale: Experimental evidence from FAFSA completion campaigns
papers.venue: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: Two RCTs reaching 800,000 students: national and state nudge campaigns had no effect on aid or enrollment.

papers.title: A National-Level Informational Experiment to Promote Enrollment in Selective Colleges
papers.venue: Journal of Policy Analysis and Management
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: RCT, 785,000 students: brochures, emails, texts, and fee waivers did not change enrollment.

papers.title: Digital Messaging to Improve College Enrollment and Success
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: Cluster RCTs: national texting was mostly null; school-based texting from students' own counselors in Texas raised college steps and enrollment for some groups.

papers.title: Customized Nudging to Improve FAFSA Completion and Income Verification
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: Multidistrict experiment: personalized texts using FAFSA status data improved completion and college matriculation.

papers.title: Parental Influences on Postsecondary Decision Making: Evidence From a Text Messaging Experiment
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: RCT: text outreach raised on-time enrollment 3.1 points; adding parents did not add effect.

papers.title: How an Artificially Intelligent Virtual Assistant Helps Students Navigate the Road to College
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: Field experiment: an AI text chatbot helped admitted students finish pre-enrollment tasks; on-time enrollment up 3.3 percentage points with less staff time.

papers.title: Summer nudging: Can personalized text messages and peer mentor outreach increase college going among low-income high school graduates?
papers.venue: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
papers.caveat: Single trial; check setting and grade band.
papers.finding: RCT: automated personalized texts and peer mentor outreach in the summer after graduation raised college enrollment for students with less counseling access.

children.name: Reminders That Work, and Reminders That Do Not
children.blurb: This idea is that reminders to students work when they come from someone the student knows, such as their own counselor, and when they name the student's actual next step.

children.name: Where the Counselor's Time Goes
children.blurb: This idea is that counselors lose too much time to scheduling, paperwork, testing coordination, and routine questions, and AI can take on some of that work.

children.name: Scholarships and Scams
children.blurb: Scholarships and Scams is about helping students find legitimate college money while avoiding fraudulent offers.

children.name: Financial Aid in Plain Language
children.blurb: Financial aid in plain language means using AI to help draft clear guides to the FAFSA and to explain common problems, while keeping official details tied to Federal Student Aid at studentaid.gov.

children.name: Keeping Seniors on Track Over the Summer
children.blurb: Keeping seniors on track over the summer means using outreach, such as texts and peer or chatbot support, to help graduating students complete enrollment tasks after counselors are no longer in regular contact.

children.name: Course Plans and Graduation Audits
children.blurb: Course plans and graduation audits are two linked counseling practices.

children.name: Exploring Colleges, Careers, Trades, and the Military
children.blurb: This idea is that college and career exploration should cover four year colleges, trade programs, apprenticeships, community colleges, and military service, with every path treated with respect.

children.name: Essays, Resumes, and Interviews
children.blurb: This idea sets out how AI may and may not be used when students write college essays, build resumes and practise interviews.

children.name: Recommendation Letters
children.blurb: AI can help a counselor or teacher draft the structure of a recommendation letter or suggest ways to describe a student's strengths, but the specific stories and details that make a letter meaningful must come from the writer.

children.name: Supporting First Generation Families
children.blurb: Supporting first generation families means giving students whose parents did not attend college and their families clear help with applications, financial aid, and campus life.

children.name: Postsecondary Planning for Students With Disabilities
children.blurb: Postsecondary planning for students with disabilities means connecting their transition plans to goals after high school and preparing them for a different accommodations system.

children.name: Guarding Against Steering
children.blurb: Guarding against steering means watching whether college and career guidance tools push students toward some paths and away from others, often repeating old patterns.

children.name: Tracking Outcomes
children.blurb: Tracking outcomes means a school uses a reporting service to learn whether its graduates enrolled in college and whether they stayed enrolled.

sections.body: Counseling, college, and career is the part of school life where students get help finishing applications, financial aid steps, course plans, and the move from high school to what comes next. The book describes summer melt, the pattern where admitted graduates plan to attend college but never show up in the fall. In one trial, an AI text chatbot sent admitted students reminders and answered questions about enrollment steps, and on time enrollment rose by 3.3 percentage points while using less staff time than human outreach. Counselors often carry very heavy caseloads, many above the 250 per counselor recommended by the American School Counselor Association, so students with the least help at home can get the least help at school. AI can help counselors reach more students with timely reminders and good information, and this chapter covers deadlines, financial aid, summer support, course planning, graduation audits, college and career exploration, essays and applications, and first generation families.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book finds that personal messages from a student's own school, tied to the student's real situation, have improved college steps and enrollment. National campaigns that sent generic messages to hundreds of thousands of students had no effect, and the difference is the connection to a real counselor and real deadlines. The common failure pattern is a district signing up for a service that sends the same messages to every student, counting messages sent as success, and seeing no change in outcomes. The rule the book holds to is that AI can widen what counselors can do, but only when it reaches the students who need help most, and counselors must approve every course plan and graduation audit. The Thirty Day Move is to set up personal, counselor sent reminders for this year's seniors, tied to real FAFSA status and application deadlines, with summer check ins and a named staff member monitoring replies, and extra support for first generation families in their own languages.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Pages like Reminders That Work, and Reminders That Do Not and Where the Counselor's Time Goes set the frame for leaders, showing the difference between personal counselor sent reminders and generic campaigns and the caseload pressure that makes reach matter. A counselor or parent would go to Financial Aid in Plain Language and Keeping Seniors on Track Over the Summer for the financial aid steps and summer check ins that keep seniors moving, while Scholarships and Scams and Supporting First Generation Families speak to money questions and extra support in families' own languages. Course Plans and Graduation Audits is where the counselor's approval role lives, and Exploring Colleges, Careers, Trades, and the Military, Essays, Resumes, and Interviews, and Recommendation Letters cover the exploration and application tasks students work through. Postsecondary Planning for Students With Disabilities and Guarding Against Steering address students who need specific planning and the risk of steering. Tracking Outcomes is the page for the board question, because it holds the enrollment, persistence, FAFSA, and summer outreach evidence by student group that shows whether the support is reaching everyone.
